anomalies.observed: U1 pin 2 (EN) has a no-connect marker and is not driven.
anomalies.expected: The TPS62933 enable input must be asserted to turn on the buck converter; the specification says U1 converts +24V to +5V.

evidence.quote: U1 TPS62933 pin 2 EN is marked no-connect (sheet 1, page 1).
U1 — TPS62933 (TI) | 24 V → 5 V synchronous buck regulator, 3 A

anomalies.impact: With EN left open, the buck converter is disabled, so the board's +5V rail and downstream +3V3 rail will not be powered as intended.

anomalies.observed: The schematic connects the LiDAR module pins to H1, with VCC on +5V, SDA/SCL on the I2C bus, and GND on ground.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes PR1 as unwired, with all four pins free and the LiDAR not connected to any net.

evidence.quote: PR1 LiDAR pins VCC, SDA, SCL, and GND are wired to H1 and the +5V, I2C_SDA, I2C_SCL, and GND nets (sheet 1, page 1).
all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.

anomalies.impact: The board provides power and an I2C connection for a LiDAR that the specified design leaves unwired and that the firmware does not support; an attached module could load or affect the I2C bus.

parsed.summary: The TPS62933 enable pin is explicitly left unconnected, preventing the specified 24-to-5 V supply from starting. The drawing also wires the LiDAR to power and I2C despite the specification stating that it is unwired.
